title: Chandrababu Naidu Meets Union Finance Minister, Seeks Immediate Release Of Funds For Cyclone Relief... - Deccan Chronicle

During a meeting with Sitharaman in New Delhi on Tuesday, Naidu explained that a preliminary assessment has put the combined losses at over `7,000 crore. He sought the Centre's intervention to expedite financial assistance, stating that immediate support was essential to accelerate relief, rehabilitation and restoration works.
Finance minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior officials participated in the meeting.
The CM said standing crops, many of which were ready for harvesting, had been submerged in floodwaters, causing huge losses to farmers. Despite the impact of El Niño, the government had ensured irrigation supplies to several areas through the Pattiseema project, but the cyclones had dealt a severe blow to the farming community. Coastal infrastructure had also suffered extensive damage, with the power distribution network among the worst-affected sectors, he said.
Naidu informed Sitharaman that central teams had already visited the state to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports shortly. He requested the Centre to consider the prevailing situation and release assistance without delay.
The CM also sought financial support for region-specific development initiatives covering Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati, aimed at accelerating economic growth and creating employment opportunities.
Referring to the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, for which Sitharaman had earlier laid the foundation stone, Naidu sought the release of funds for infrastructure development. He said the state government was focusing on improving rural road connectivity, strengthening irrigation facilities and promoting drip irrigation to boost horticulture and agricultural productivity in the region.
Naidu also sought additional central assistance for developing the Visakhapatnam Economic Region, which was witnessing rapid growth. Though the region had received support from the Centre through various channels, further financial assistance would help accelerate its development and extend its benefits to more people. The release of Purvodaya funds and key decisions announced at the recently concluded CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam also figured in the discussions.
Sitharaman described the proposed Investment Protection Act as a revolutionary initiative and appreciated the government's plan to establish escrow accounts for industrial incentives. She observed that these measures would bring transformative changes to the investment ecosystem, strengthen industrialists' confidence and help attract more investments to Andhra Pradesh.
